To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
epileptiform activity can be induced in human hippocampal granule cell populations by high K+ in vitro and that the pattern of epileptiform discharges is related to hippocampal sclerosis.

(i) ictaform activities can be elicited in human dentate gyrus (DG) slices from patients with and without hippocampal sclerosis (HS); (ii) the pattern of icts and their threshold to induction differ between the two groups; and (iii) the ictaforms in slices from scleroic hippocampi were characterized by stimulus-induced oscillatory field potentials.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether granule cells in hippocampal specimens resectioned for medically intractable epilepsy are capable of generating epileptiform activity.
the development of ictal discharges in human epileptic tissue and their dependence on the underlying morphological substrate.
the development of a new class of granule cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a network of granule cell axons in the supragranular zone is a necessary, but insufficient, condition to induce epileptiform activity in the human dentate gyrus.

, in TLE patients with hippocampal sclerosis and aberrant mossy fiber sproutings, high K+-evoked seizure-like activity in granule cell networks is more easily evoked, more pronounced, and more likely to develop into a sustained epileptic activity.
the presence of aberrantly sprouted mossy fibers is a necessary but not sufficient condition for the generation of epileptiform activity in the human dentate gyrus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in granule cell population of human hippocampal slices with hippocampal sclerosis and mossy fiber re-organization, high potassium concentration induced seizure-like activity, which was sensitive to glutamatergic receptor blockade and lowering of extracellular calcium.

, in the human dentate gyrus, ictaform and seizure-like activity is not a unique feature of the epileptogenic hippocampi but is also present in nonsclerotic ones, albeit with different electrophysiological characteristics.
the presence of mossy fiber sprouts is not a prerequisite for the induction of epileptiform activity in the human dentate gyrus.
The main takeaway from our work is that

epileptic activity in the dentate gyrus of patients with TLE is highly sensitive to changes in the extracellular potassium concentration and that the epileptic threshold in the dentate is significantly lowered when mossy fiber sprouts are present.
the presence of aberrantly sprouted mossy fibers in the human dentate gyrus is not sufficient to trigger seizure-like activity in the granule cell layer.

the epileptogenic threshold of human granule cells can be modulated in a way similar to that of rodent dentate gyrus, and this modulation is associated with a network reorganization that is a hallmark of human hippocampal sclerosis.
